### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **24** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/runtime.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**21** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6ff3eee7ca595cf1bb5c47e9fc09bb127c0a57d0`.

⛔ **9** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/runtime.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **173** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6ff3eee7ca595cf1bb5c47e9fc09bb127c0a57d0` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `eea65925b461acffe19e0618c5cfa81640cb921b` — the merge of head `763105ecec86da5d14ba9b8d70c55e1644ff7e49` into base `6ff3eee7ca595cf1bb5c47e9fc09bb127c0a57d0`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin eea65925b461acffe19e0618c5cfa81640cb921b && git checkout eea65925b461acffe19e0618c5cfa81640cb921b
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 6ff3eee7ca595cf1bb5c47e9fc09bb127c0a57d0 763105ecec86da5d14ba9b8d70c55e1644ff7e49 && git checkout -B drift-repro 6ff3eee7ca595cf1bb5c47e9fc09bb127c0a57d0 && git merge --no-ff 763105ecec86da5d14ba9b8d70c55e1644ff7e49

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6ff3eee7ca595cf1bb5c47e9fc09bb127c0a57d0
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 6ff3eee7ca595cf1bb5c47e9fc09bb127c0a57d0` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `763105ecec86da5d14ba9b8d70c55e1644ff7e49`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.object-extension-formula-cycle-refused.ts + packages/lint/src/object-graph.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.ts, packages/lint/src/formula-cycle-issues.ts, packages/lint/src/runtime-gate.ts, packages/lint/src/authoring-rules.ts, packages/lint/src/runtime.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-authoring-gate.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/runtime-authoring-gate.ts

PR #33702 for card #33494. Inputs read: the card body and its five comments (carry note 6886038545, claim 6888533455, surface amendment 6888588670, dev report 6890640694), the PR body and file list (16 files), the net diff against `main`, and the check-runs on the head. The rest of the diff (five test files, the changeset, `content/docs/deployment/validating-metadata.mdx`) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`; the tests were read only as evidence for the pins.

**Check-runs on the head (64):** 21 success, 10 skipped, 0 failed, 33 with no conclusion yet at review time (15 in progress, 18 queued). Concluded green: Check Changeset, PR-body guards, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Spec property liveness, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests, Check Documentation Links, Check PR Size, Dogfood Regression Gate. Not yet concluded: Build Core, Test Core 1-8, Type Check (workspace, consumer gates, debt ledger), Lint (CI release and engine gates, query-options erasure), Live E2E UI, Type Check UI, Build and E2E UI, Test UI 1-16. This record judges the contract; it does not stand in for those verdicts, and landing waits for them to conclude green.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Door accept-set, shape 1 (tie) and shape 2 (outranked): widened. Right.** `objectsAsServed(stack, storedExtensions)` puts a name whose deciding writers share a priority in `tied`, `objectsWithoutTiedFields` drops it, and the fill-back from `base` skips every name a stored entry adds, so the tied name is absent from `fieldDefs` and no cycle is found. With a sibling at 300 over the entry at 200 the sibling's definition is the one in `fieldDefs`, and `extensionFormulaLoci` deletes the entry's locus for that name. Both are the build's verdict.
2. **Door accept-set, shape 3 (false negative): narrowed. Right.** The sibling's `s__c` formula is served over the entry's `s__c`, the entry's `a__c` stays the entry's, the cycle is found and reported on `a__c` alone (the only name with a locus). The build reports the same member at the same entry, plus the sibling's member at the sibling's entry, which is not this write's.
3. **`os build`, `os validate`, `os lint`: unchanged. Right.** No build caller passes `stored`; both fold functions default it to `[]`, and `storedExtensions` is `[]` unless `runtimeWriteType` is `object_extension`.
4. **Baseline pass of the door's differential: unchanged. Right.** With the stored list and no written entry the walk visits the target, skips every stored entry, and `extensionFormulaLoci` returns an empty map, so nothing is reported in either pass for a sibling's own state.
5. **Published surface: additive only. Right.** `storedObjectExtensions?` on `runRuntimeAuthoringRules`, `evaluateRuntimeAuthoringGate`, `AuthoringRuleContext` and `StackExpressionOptions`; a defaulted second parameter on `objectExtensionsByTarget` and `objectsAsServed`; `stored?: true` on `VisibleObjectExtension`; the `StoredObjectExtension` type exported from `@objectstack/lint/runtime`; the new export `otherPackagesExtensionsOf`. Nothing is removed or made required. A host that states nothing gets the previous reading (pinned by the "states no extensions" case).
6. **One fold. Right.** The door's ranking is `objectExtensionsByTarget` and `objectsAsServed` with the host's entries added to their input through the fold's own `collect`; sort, replacement and the tie set are the build's lines. `otherPackagesExtensionsOf` only lists contributors; it ranks nothing.
7. **Disabled packages. Right.** `otherPackagesExtensionsOf` leaves out `ownership === 'extend'` contributors whose `isPackageDisabled(packageId)` is true, the same predicate `withholdDisabledExtensions` applies on the served fold that builds the door's target (`resolveObjectLeavingExtensionsOut`). So the stored list and the served target leave out the same entries. The build has no disabled state; the amendment's phrase "as the build leaves them out" is met in the only sense available, a disabled package's entry takes no part in the fold.
8. **No `packages/spec` schema moves. Right.** The spec file in the diff is the semantic entry's text only.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/33494-extension-door-priority-fold.md`: `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` and `@objectstack/spec` at `minor`. Matches what the diff publishes: the kind is `narrowed` (shape 3 is a value newly refused at a door), which takes at least `minor` on each package the diff moves, and the diff moves all three (spec through the entry's text).

`Clause-②: no (narrowing)` is right: one shape narrows, and the closed pair gives `(narrowing)` when a narrowing is present; the two widenings are stated in the same line and in the BREAKING banner. `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` is right by the precedence rule (narrowed over semantic over added). Both lines are in the PR body and the changeset body and agree. The title carries `!`. The ADR-0087 marker `not-required (already-registered object-extension-formula-cycle-refused)` is right: entry 18 is unreleased (its registering changeset `33153-extension-formula-cycle.md` is still pending in the tree) and this PR rewrites it in place. The banner has Before, Now, Unchanged and Fix, and the Fix sentence gives the author's remedy for the narrowed shape.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **`open_questions`:** none in the dev report.
- **Deviation: metadata-protocol gate files added.** Ruled by the seat's amendment 6888588670. Answered.
- **Deviation: `packages/runtime/src/domains/meta-object-extension-item.test.ts` edited.** A test file; the amendment dropped the runtime source line, not its tests. Accepted.
- **Deviation: two lint meta-test tables (`storedNames`, `stored`).** Required by the receiver scans; test files. Accepted.
- **Deviation: `validate-expressions.ts` ~:2391 edited.** Allowed by the amendment; `origin/main` with PR #33434 is merged into the head, and both edits are on the merged line.
- **Carry note 6886038545, item 1** (the 33153 changeset's "the written definition is the one served"): answered. That file is another PR's and is not edited; the new changeset's Now paragraph quotes and corrects the clause and the Unchanged sentence.
- **Carry note 6886038545, item 2** ("at the same priority" should read "at the priority that decides it"): answered in the entry, the docs paragraph, the call-site comment and the changeset.
- **Out-of-scope edge the dev reported: out of scope, not a must-fix.** Two parts:
  - *The tie itself.* A field two packages add at the deciding priority is judged at neither seam. That is the card's shape 1 as ruled: the card asks the door to give the build's verdict, and the build cannot judge a tie because the stack does not state registration order. Observation for the seat, not a finding on this PR: at the door the registry does know the order (a republished entry is pushed last and the priority sort is stable, so the written definition wins a tie until the next boot reorders it), so a self-reading formula on a tied name can now publish and be served. Closing that means judging ties at the door differently from the build, which is the opposite of this card's TO. If it is wanted, it is a new card with its own ruling.
  - *The corner the dev named.* When the target's owner also declares the tied name, the build fills the name back from the authored object and can refuse a cycle through the owner's definition; the door carries only the served target, skips the name, and accepts. It needs an owner formula field that two packages both redefine at the deciding priority plus a cycle through it, and the definition the build judges there is one the registry does not serve. It is outside the card's three shapes, was present in the build before this PR, and the door's reading is the one the entry states. File it as a follow-up card (p3 or lower); see nit 1.

### ④ Design judgment

**`18.object-extension-formula-cycle-refused.ts` (hits).** Read against the walk in `validate-expressions.ts`, the fold in `object-graph.ts`, and the registry (`registerObject`'s `extend` arm, `withholdDisabledExtensions`, `registerObjectExtension`) in the live tree.

- "The publish door folds the written entry among the other packages' published extensions of its target by priority, as `os build` folds every package's entry": true; one fold, the host's entries added to its input.
- "the written entry's where its priority decides the field, another package's where that one outranks it (a cycle that definition closes through another field of the written entry is refused on that field)": true; `extensionFormulaLoci` leaves a locus only on names the written entry decides, and `formulaCycleIssues` reports only names with a locus.
- "One exception holds on an object the stack declares (at the door, one the deployment serves): a field two packages' extensions add at the priority that decides it is not judged": true at the door (the fill-back skip). True of the build except in the owner-declared corner (nit 1).
- "(on an object the stack does not declare the later entry's definition is judged)": true at both; at the door stored entries carry carriers below 0, so the written entry is the later one at an equal priority.
- `acceptanceCriteria`, "which neither the build nor the door judges": true, with the same corner.
- The entry's default priority (200) matches `DEFAULT_EXTENDER_PRIORITY`, and `StoredObjectExtension.priority` absent reads as 200 through the fold's own default.

**Attempts to break it, none of which did:**
- Three packages: two siblings tied at 300 over the entry at 200 (tied, dropped); a sibling at 300 over a 200/200 tie (`tiedKeys.delete`, sibling served). Both are the build's result.
- A sibling below the entry whose formula reads a field of the entry that reads it back: found, reported on the entry's field only.
- A sibling's own stored cycle, tied or not: no locus, never charged to the write (pinned).
- A registry that cannot answer, or a contributor list that throws: `[]`, the previous reading.
- The written package's own stored extension: left out by `packageId === writtenPackage`, the same id `withoutExtensionsOf` removes from the served target.
- Stored `fields` as a record keyed by name: `recordsOf` gives each its name.

**Implementing files, sentence by sentence.** `object-graph.ts`, `validate-expressions.ts`, `formula-cycle-issues.ts`, `runtime-gate.ts`, `authoring-rules.ts`, `runtime.ts`, `protocol-authoring-gate.ts`, `runtime-authoring-gate.ts`: each jsdoc and comment the diff adds or rewrites agrees with the code beside it. The list is read on an `object_extension` write only at both `runtime-gate.ts` and `validate-expressions.ts`.

**Pins.** The #33153 pin "the door judges the written entry's own definition whatever a sibling's priority" is replaced; shapes 1 and 2 now assert no finding at the door and none in the build; shape 3 asserts a refusal at the door on `a__c` with the engine's sentence, and the build's two locations. The dev report gives shape 3 and shapes 1/2 red over the base sources, and three ablations each turning the matching case red. The runtime describe pins the same three shapes through `saveMetaItem` and `publishMetaItem`, with a control. The pins move to the build's verdict and shape 3 is pinned red.

**Findings.**

1. **nit** — In the owner-declared corner (③, second part) the build still judges a tied name, as the owner's definition, so "neither the build nor the door judges" and "both judge the same definition of each field" are not exact of the build there. The text is right for the door, the build's behaviour predates this PR, and no verdict on the card's three shapes depends on it. Leave as an accepted deviation and carry it on the follow-up card.
2. **nit** — `otherPackagesExtensionsOf` reads contributors under the target the body names and does not mirror the registry's legacy `NS__NAME` filing (`extensionTargetKey`, #28858). On such a target the list is empty and the door reads as before this PR. The lint fold already documents the same gap, and the PR's acceptance notes state it. Accepted deviation.

No must-fix, no should-fix.
